title: O statua gentilissima
subtitle: Leporello, Don Giovanni and the Commendatore: duet from Don Giovanni, Act 2 (No. 22)

passages.label: O statua gentilissima · Finiscila, o nel petto · Che gusto! che spassetto!
O statua gentilissima, benchè di marmo · Padron mio! mirate! · Mori! · No, no, attendete!
Signor, il padron mio · vorria con voi cenar · Ah! che scena è questa! · chinò la testa!
Va là, che sei un buffone · Guardate ancor, padrone! · E che deggio guardar?
Colla marmorea testa · Parlate! se potete · Verrete a cena? · Sì!
Mover mi posso appena · Bizarra è in ver la scena · andiamo via di quà (to the end)

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Don Giovanni, K. 527 (1787), Act 2 scene 12 (the churchyard), No. 22 Duet
licences.author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

licences.source: Lorenzo Da Ponte, libretto of Don Giovanni (1787)
licences.author: Lorenzo Da Ponte (1749–1838)
licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score ("Io sento mi gelar" for sentomi; "questo acciar" for quest'acciar; "o ciel" and "o Dei" for Oh ciel / oh Dei; "che sei un buffone" for se'; "Bizarra è in ver" for Bizzarra è inver; quà; the score's repeats of words and lines).

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 245–250, bars 1–108 of No. 22
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics, slurs and other marks, settled against a third independent reading, then checked bar by bar and checked again by fresh checkers, whose finding (a staccato removed in bar 96) was corrected. The English singing translation, the stage directions and the instrument cues are left out. Allegro, 4/4, 108 full bars. Playback tempo: ♩ = 126, about 3:26, from the median of five complete recordings (Giulini 1959 3:37, Fricsay 1958 3:26, Klemperer 1966 3:35, C. Davis 1973 3:18, Haitink 1984 3:22; median 3:26). Mozart gives the word Allegro only.
